doc.title: Jimmy Cobb — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Massimo's Italian school and other clinics
summary: Cobb describes the Italian clinic faculty and master classes.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Hal. Kind of an older saxophone player.
Oh, Hal – you know, from California. He used to play with Max. Harold Land. Is that who you’re talking about? Not Harold Land.
But he’d just bring guys over on different instruments to teach Italian guys.
Shawnn Monteiro. She’s a singer. Sings like Carmen.
Shawnn Monteiro is a singer that actually was Jimmy . . .
. . . Woode’s daughter. You know Jimmy Woode?
She sings, and she teaches a class over there. So he brings people like that. They have it every year or something like that. So we do that.
And I did a thing at Berklee.
Guys call me from different places to do little clinics.
That’s what happens. When they call up, we do them if it’s possible.
We like to do it every time there’s a gig. We like to somehow get the school involved and do a master class. It’s work.
